base: Use registration.baseline generator and its original two incident-family indices 4 and 5. For each split, draw 0 upward, LONDON then NETHERLANDS per draw; each successive twelve draws in one family form a quota block. Preserve the original cell order randomization, private incident truth law, generator's shared twin token, automatic protection, original maintenance allocation and public evidence generation.
experimental_population: Synthetic shifts and signed write windows vary. This registers a new work-schedule distribution on the frozen facility. It covers ordinary, insufficient evidence, adverse and infeasible cells from the base law, independently of any policy score. The altered times are operational requests to actual work/admission interfaces; no row-specific identity marker is appended to an input.

operative_variations.apply: The profile determines two real public and operational staff shift intervals [60*start,60*end] in native.dispatch_program.public.workforce.shifts. Apply through the original workforce interface, binding the identical intervals to admission, execution and the worker's public calendar. Preserve all remaining professionals' original shifts and all time/permit endpoint conventions. A delayed start or earlier end can change which work can actually be completed.
operative_variations.permit: For each original subject whose public write_window=[a,b] has b−a >= 3*60, set its upper endpoint to min(3600,max(a+60,b+60*j)), preserving a. All shorter, expired and locked windows, including [1,2], keep their original bytes. Use one profile offset j across eligible subjects of this condition, identically for each paired arm. Public orders, actual grant checks and the scorer must use the same admitted schedule. A permission does not alter the facility's true ability to complete the work.

deterministic_selection.seeds: Use the split's own 32-byte seed per seed-registration.json. Only the curator supplies the unsigned big-endian integer to the original inputs_v3.condition with the original draw and templates. No generator, private template, seed or family index is available to a policy or improver.
deterministic_selection.canonical_hash: H(tag,seedhex,family,value) = SHA-256 of UTF-8 canonical JSON array [tag,lowercase_seed_hex,family,value] with sorted object keys, compact separators, ASCII escaping and no LF. Lexicographic comparisons use digest bytes.
deterministic_selection.assignment: For each family, enumerate the Cartesian product of the two start grids and two end grids in schedule_tuple_order. For DEV remove that family's profile tuples already used in FIT, irrespective of results. Sort remaining tuples by (H('AegisDC/T8/r0/profile/v1',split_seed,family,tuple),tuple). Traverse blocks in increasing order. In each block allocate the next distinct tuple to each of the 11 schedule groups in this fixed order: NORMAL, FALSE_NOTICE, SAFE_TRANSFER, TWIN_PAIR, EARLY_ALARM, SILENT, LATE, LOCKED, SPECIAL_A, SPECIAL_B, PARTIAL. Both original TWIN_A and TWIN_B take TWIN_PAIR. For the remaining ten cells take their named group. Preserve the source generator's shuffled slot order when serializing the conditions. Group names remain private. Sort j in the declared offset grid by (H('AegisDC/T8/r0/window/v1',split_seed,family,[tuple,j]),j), select its first entry, and apply the public permit-end rule. BASE physical truth parameters and challenge times remain paired to the unmodified source case.
deterministic_selection.reason: A new seed alone does not prevent repeated small finite input combinations. Without-replacement profiles vary actual staff availability and eligibility while the paired twins retain their common public schedule. The block remains the analysis unit. The finite schedule pool and quota constraints make the t-reference power an approximation; its empirical coverage on wider distributions is unknown.
deterministic_selection.future_qualification: Before any scored FIT run, under a separate implementation authorization, verify the schedule round trip into both the real and public workforce gate, unchanged hard constraints and locked windows, twin schedule equality, nonoperative metadata removal, regeneration of public research data only, indistinguishability before evidence, and fixture cases allowing both valid action and valid waiting. No fixture or policy has been executed by r0.

entries.scope: T5 v3a panel; v3b reuses these rows
T5 v3c old panel (v3a) and new panel
T7 stage 1 original incident rows, T3 aliases
H3 pre-score index only, isolated principal
entries.allowed_input: The controller receives presealed per-row full and operative hash columns only. No H3 case, score, trace, result or raw seed. Do not open this index during r0.

historical_catalogue.coverage: Before either scoring release the curator reconciles each original manifest, technical fixture wrapper and every recorded reused/probe or extension panel with its signed inventory. Use the recorded original case behind T3 engineering input and T4c engineering case wrappers. Keep aliases and prove equality; repeated use of the same condition is one old identity. Missing, incomparable or unaccounted realized inputs block release. Earlier indices and H3 data never enter development images, FIT feedback, DEV policies or per-row public novelty replies.
historical_catalogue.common_old_schema: Compare the original full and comparable operative forms prescribed in design.json. For T3's maintenance-free core only, project {native,attachment} symmetrically. In a v3 case normalize only each signed order whose value exactly equals OPEN/MAINT-<that case's declared exposure_s> to the T3 value OPEN before hashing this ADDITIONAL cross-version core projection. In T3 retain OPEN. All other public times, shifts, grants, evidence, physics and actions are preserved. This additional test can exclude a case even when its v3 maintenance differs; it cannot weaken the full or v3 operative tests. Never reconstruct an H3 row to obtain a new projection.

release: One signed allow/stop receipt per complete split before scoring, per design.json. Full and operative overlap must both be zero against all registered prior inputs, within split and across FIT/DEV. A blocked batch, partial reference index or unauthorized read leaves that split unscored and halts this attempt; no redraw. Actual overlap is UNTESTED at r0.
